title: Design Spec: Console Usage Insights — Route + Model Cost Drivers
author: Tessa Morgan
body:
## Summary
This design spec defines the Console information architecture and key interaction patterns for **Usage Insights** focused on attributing **cost + latency** to **developer-defined routes** and **model variants**.

Primary outcomes:
- Customers can quickly answer: “Which routes cost the most?”, “Which models drive that spend?”, and “What changed vs last week?”
- UI supports *exploration* (filters, sorting, drilldowns) and *operations workflows* (exportable reports).
- UI remains usable under cardinality constraints (many routes, missing tags, normalization/hashing).

This spec covers:
- IA, pages, and navigation
- Route list and route detail views
- Filter model and global controls
- Empty states and error states
- Pagination/limits and performance requirements
- Accessibility requirements and test notes

Non-goals for this spec:
- Full anomaly detection/alerting UX (beyond “change vs prior period” deltas)
- Customer-configurable arbitrary custom dimensions beyond route/model
- Long-term historical export flows beyond the product retention policy

---

## Users & use cases
### Primary personas
1) **Engineering/ML** (building features, debugging cost regressions)
- Wants route-level visibility to tie spend to product surfaces.
- Needs model breakdown and latency/error correlation.

2) **FinOps / Ops** (chargeback, budgeting, procurement)
- Needs exports suitable for spreadsheets and internal reporting.
- Needs consistent definitions and reconciliation guidance.

3) **Platform teams** (multi-service deployments)
- Needs environment/region/deployment-mode segmentation.
- Needs guardrails to keep route naming sane.

### Core jobs-to-be-done
- Identify top routes by spend in a time window.
- Drill into a route to understand which models and token types drive cost.
- Compare period-over-period to see what changed.
- Export a bounded report for review/audit.

---

## Information architecture (IA)
### Placement in Console
Proposed nav:
- **Console → Observability → Usage Insights**
  - (Tab) **Routes** (default)
  - (Tab) **Models** (future; not required for GA but reserved in IA)

Rationale:
- Usage Insights is an Observability-adjacent view (cost + performance). Users expect it near metrics/tracing.
- “Routes” is the first-class entry point for “cost drivers by endpoint”.

### Page list
1) **Usage Insights / Routes (List)**
- Table of routes ranked by spend
- Inline trend (sparkline)
- Filters and grouping controls
- Export entry point

2) **Usage Insights / Route Detail**
- Route header with key metrics and deltas vs prior period
- Model breakdown section
- Time series section (cost and latency)
- “Data notes” panel (route normalization, missing tags, freshness)
- Export action scoped to this route

### Breadcrumb + deep links
- Breadcrumb: Observability → Usage Insights → Routes → {Route name}
- All views support URL state to share:
  - time range
  - filters (env, region, deployment mode, org/project)
  - selected route
  - selected comparison mode

---

## Global controls & filter model
### Shared global filter bar
Applies to Routes list and Route detail.

Controls (left → right):
1) **Time range**
- Presets: Last 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d (default), 30d
- Custom range picker (bounded by retention policy)

2) **Compare to** (period-over-period)
- Off (default for very short ranges like 1h)
- Previous period (same length)
- Previous week (only enabled when range ≥ 24h)

3) **Environment**
- Values: Production, Staging, Development (configurable list; default: Production)

4) **Region**
- Multi-select
- Default: All regions

5) **Deployment mode**
- Hosted API, Dedicated, Private
- Default: All

6) **Project**
- Single-select within the active org
- Default: “All projects” if user has access

7) **Search**
- Search routes by route name
- Supports prefix match and contains

### Filter behavior notes
- All filters are “AND” combined.
- The UI must show a **filter summary** in the export confirmation (human readable).
- If a filter combination yields no results, show an empty state (see Empty States).

### Route and model terminology
- **Route**: Canonical route identifier (SDK-provided preferred; gateway-derived fallback). Normalization rules are defined by the ADR.
- **Model**: Model identifier displayed as {family}/{variant} with optional suffix for quantization/profile.

Display rules:
- If route is missing → display as **Unknown route** with tooltip explaining how to set route tags.
- If model is missing/obfuscated due to policy → display as **Unknown model**.

---

## Routes List view
### Purpose
Answer “What routes are costing me the most?” with fast scanning, filtering, and drill-down.

### Layout
Header:
- Title: “Usage Insights — Routes”
- Subtitle: “Cost and performance by route”
- Right side: Export button

Body:
- Global filter bar (sticky)
- Table with ranking + sparklines

### Table columns (v1)
1) **Route**
- Route name (normalized)
- Secondary line: route source badge (SDK / Gateway / Unknown) when available
- Tooltip: normalization hints + “View naming guidance” link

2) **Total cost**
- Currency display (USD by default; respects org billing currency)
- Shows delta vs comparison period as % and absolute ($)

3) **Tokens (in / out / cached)**
- Compact display e.g. “12.4M / 8.1M / 3.2M” with tooltip and expanded breakdown

4) **Unit cost**
- Primary: $ / 1K tokens (or org setting)
- Tooltip: definition and caveats (cached tokens, late metering)

5) **Latency p95**
- ms value
- Delta vs comparison period (optional; only if compare enabled)

6) **Error rate**
- % value
- Tooltip: which status codes included

7) **Trend**
- Sparkline for cost over the selected time window
- Hover reveals min/max and last datapoint

### Default sorting
- Default sort: **Total cost (desc)**.
- Secondary sorts available: latency p95, error rate, unit cost.

### Row interactions
- Clicking a row navigates to Route Detail.
- Route name is a link; whole row is clickable for usability.

### Bulk and “Top N” behavior
- Default page size: 50 rows.
- Maximum page size options: 25 / 50 / 100.
- Route list queries should cap at **Top 5,000 routes** per filter set; beyond that, show a message:
  - “Showing top 5,000 routes. Refine filters or search to narrow results.”

### “Other” aggregation (optional, recommended)
To reduce visual noise, optionally include a final row:
- **Other (aggregated)**: sums for all routes beyond Top N
- This row is not clickable.

Design note: If backend does not support “Other” at GA, omit rather than approximating in UI.

---

## Route Detail view
### Purpose
Answer “Why is this route expensive and what changed?”

### Layout
1) **Header**
- Route name
- Badges: env / region / deployment mode (from filters), plus “route source”
- Quick actions: Export, Copy deep link

2) **Summary cards (top row)**
- Total cost
- Tokens (in/out/cached)
- Unit cost
- Latency p95
- Error rate

Each summary card shows:
- Primary value for selected time range
- Delta vs comparison period (if enabled)
- Small caption: “vs previous period” / “vs previous week”

3) **Model breakdown section**
- Stacked bar or table (see below)

4) **Time series section**
- Cost over time (line)
- Latency p95 over time (line)
- Error rate over time (line)

5) **Data notes & troubleshooting panel** (right rail or collapsible)
- Freshness/lag indicator
- Route naming and normalization summary
- Link to docs: route tagging best practices
- Link to “Known issues: cost mismatches”

### Model breakdown (recommended UI)
Default representation: **Table with small bar visualization** for share-of-cost.

Columns:
- Model
- Total cost
- Share of route cost (%)
- Tokens (in/out/cached)
- Unit cost
- Latency p95
- Error rate

Interactions:
- Toggle: “Show top 10 models” / “Show all” (with max cap)
- Click model row to apply a local filter (Model = X) that updates the charts below

If many models are present (fallback/routing behavior):
- Cap at Top 100 models by cost (per route). Show “Showing top 100 models” message.

### “What changed” guidance
A dedicated “What changed” callout appears when compare is enabled:
- Shows top 3 contributors to cost delta:
  1) Token volume change
  2) Model mix change
  3) Unit cost change

This is explanatory text with computed values from backend deltas where possible; otherwise show a simplified message:
- “Cost increased primarily due to higher token volume.”

Design note: Avoid implying causal certainty without data. Use language like “primarily correlated with”.

---

## Export entry points (placement + UX)
Although export mechanics are covered in the API/security specs, the UI placement is part of this design.

### Placement
- Routes List: top-right primary button “Export”
- Route Detail: top-right secondary button “Export route report”

### Export confirmation (modal)
Modal includes:
- Format: CSV / JSON
- Scope summary:
  - Time range
  - Compare setting (if any)
  - Filters (env/region/deployment mode/project)
  - If route detail: route name
- Limits summary:
  - “Exports are bounded (row and size limits). Large time ranges may be truncated; see docs.”
- CTA: “Generate export”

### Post-action feedback
- Toast: “Export started. You can download when ready.”
- Link to “Exports” drawer/page if present; otherwise provide a single “View export status” link.

---

## Empty states & error states
### 1) No data (first-time user / no traffic)
Condition:
- Zero requests in selected time range and filters.

UI:
- Empty illustration
- Copy:
  - Title: “No usage data for this time range”
  - Body: “Try expanding the time range, selecting a different project/region, or verify traffic is reaching Redwood.”
- Helpful links:
  - “How usage insights works”
  - “Check integration / SDK setup”

### 2) Missing route tagging (Unknown route dominates)
Condition:
- “Unknown route” is > 50% of cost (threshold configurable).

UI:
- Inline banner at top of Routes List and Route Detail:
  - “Most spend is currently attributed to Unknown route. Add route identifiers to improve attribution.”
- CTA: “View route tagging guide”

### 3) Results truncated due to limits
Condition:
- Backend returns “truncated” or “limit reached” flag.

UI:
- Non-blocking inline message:
  - “Showing top results. Refine filters or shorten time range for complete breakdown.”

### 4) Partial data / freshness lag
Condition:
- Pipeline lag exceeds freshness SLO or late-arriving metering events expected.

UI:
- Badge next to time range: “Data delayed”
- Tooltip includes:
  - “Data may be delayed by up to X minutes.”
  - “Costs may change as late events arrive.”

### 5) Authorization / RBAC
Condition:
- User lacks access to selected project or export permission.

UI:
- 403 page state: “You don’t have access to Usage Insights for this project.”
- If export blocked but view allowed:
  - Disable Export button with tooltip: “Export requires the Billing Analyst role (or equivalent).”

### 6) API error / timeout
UI:
- Show error panel with:
  - “Couldn’t load usage insights.”
  - Retry button
  - “Copy error ID” for support

---

## Pagination, limits, and performance requirements
### Pagination model
- Routes list: server-side pagination (cursor or page token).
- Route detail model breakdown: server-side pagination only if “show all” exceeds threshold; otherwise capped list.

### UI constraints (v1)
- Max routes displayed: 5,000 (with search/filters to narrow)
- Max models displayed per route: 100
- Max time range selectable: per retention policy (UI should read from config)

### Performance targets (UI)
- Routes list initial load: aim for < 2.5s p95 on typical orgs
- Route detail initial load: < 3.0s p95
- Filter changes should feel responsive:
  - Show skeleton loading within 150ms
  - Prefer optimistic UI only for local interactions (sorting), not for data changes

### Loading states
- Use skeleton table rows for list page.
- Use card skeletons for summary metrics.
- Charts show lightweight shimmer placeholders.

---

## Accessibility (A11y) requirements
### General
- Meet WCAG 2.1 AA for key workflows.
- All controls accessible by keyboard.
- Visible focus states (Design System compliant).

### Tables
- Use semantic table markup (header cells, scope attributes).
- Ensure sortable columns announce sort state to screen readers.
- Row click targets must not break keyboard navigation; provide explicit link inside Route cell.

### Charts and sparklines
- Provide text alternatives:
  - Sparkline: aria-label with time range and direction (e.g., “Cost trend up 12% over 7 days”).
  - Main charts: include summary table below or “View as table” toggle for screen readers.

### Color and contrast
- Cost/latency/error colors must not be the sole indicator.
- Deltas should include arrows/text labels (Increase/Decrease) and not rely only on red/green.

### Modals (Export)
- Focus trap within modal.
- Escape closes modal.
- Clear heading and description.

---

## Copy & terminology guidelines
- Use “route” consistently; avoid mixing with “endpoint” except in guidance text.
- Use “cost” for currency-based totals; “spend” acceptable in explanatory copy.
- Use “Unknown route” (not “unattributed”) to keep the action clear.
- Prefer “comparison period” over “last week” unless it is truly previous week.

---

## Open questions / decisions needed
1) Should we include an “Other (aggregated)” row at GA? (Depends on backend support.)
2) Should Route Detail support selecting multiple models to compare? (Likely post-GA.)
3) Do we need a dedicated “Exports” center in Console for tracking/report downloads, or is toast + direct download sufficient for v1?
4) What role name is surfaced in the UI for export permissions (needs alignment with RBAC naming conventions)?

---

## Appendix: Proposed component inventory
- Global filter bar (time range, compare, env, region, deployment mode, project, search)
- Routes table (sortable, paginated)
- Metric summary cards (with deltas)
- Model breakdown table (with mini-bars)
- Time series charts (cost/latency/error)
- Export modal (format + scope summary)
- Empty state components (no data, missing route tags, truncated)

---

## Changelog
- 2026-02-06: Initial draft (IA + core views)
- 2026-02-14: Added empty states, truncation behavior, and export modal placement
- 2026-02-20: Added accessibility requirements and pagination/limits guidance
